title: Stop the sample buffer from stalling under load

blocks.text: A metrics agent keeps the latency samples it records between two flushes in a `SampleBuffer`, a growable `double[]`. On quiet nodes nobody notices it. On the busiest nodes, which record a few hundred thousand samples between flushes, the agent falls behind, and a profile shows most of its time inside `Arrays.copyOf`.

The buffer already stores, copies and counts. Finish `newCapacity(current, needed)` in `src/main/java/practice/SampleBuffer.java`: the size of the new array when the buffer is full. A buffer may be created with capacity 0, and `addAll` can bring a batch larger than the room left.
When you're done, filling a buffer with n samples copies a small multiple of n elements in total, however large n gets. About three lines in total.

cases.says: samples added one at a time are all kept, in order, as the buffer grows
a batch that needs a little more room lands after the samples already there
the capacity grows in proportion to its size, so the total copying stays a small multiple of the number of samples
a buffer created with capacity 0 still grows when the first sample arrives
one growth step makes room for a whole batch, even one larger than the proportional growth

origin.section: Amortised O(1): ArrayList.add Copies Each Element a Few Times, Not n Times

concepts: A growable array that grows its capacity in proportion to its size copies a small multiple of n elements over n adds, so add is amortised O(1); a fixed growth step makes the total O(n^2).
